note: Attacker-controlled input bytes are parsed as a serialized frame-backed super-chunk.

code: construct frame-backed schunk from the supplied buffer
note: The input buffer becomes the backing frame that later chunk reads will reference.
The fuzzer iterates through chunk indexes and asks the library to decompress each chunk from the parsed frame.
Decompression first materializes a lazy chunk pointer; the bug depends on how that pointer is obtained and later released.
For a file-backed frame, the chunk is heap-allocated and marked as requiring free before returning.
The lazy chunk trailer is synthesized from attacker-controlled frame metadata and block sizes.
After successful decompression the heap chunk is freed by the caller.
On an error path after allocation, the same heap buffer is also freed here, so a later caller free can become a double/invalid free.
